the sun reversed for him,
is probably not true!
Furthermore, the sun is fire.
Even if a sage waved away fire,
they ultimately could not repel it.
When Lǔ Yáng Gōng waved at the sun,
how could he possibly make it go back?
Sometimes, during battle, the sun was exactly at mǎo (5-7 AM).
Because of the confusion of battle,
people thought the sun was setting.
They waved at it, turning left
on a curved path, and the sun seemed to go back.
The world loves the supernatural and strange,
and therefore they said it went back.
This is not what is meant.
The *Zhuàn Shū* (Commentary) says:
"Jīng Kē, for the Crown Prince of Yān,
plotted to assassinate the King of Qín,
and a white rainbow pierced the sun.
Master Wèi, for Qín,
planned the affair at Chángpíng,
and Venus eclipsed the Pleiades."
This says that profound sincerity moves Heaven,
and Heaven causes changes.
Now, to say that
"a white rainbow pierced the sun"
and "Venus eclipsed the Pleiades"
are real.
Speaking of Jīng Kē's 荊軻 plan and
Wèi Xiānshēng's 衛先生 strategy,
to say they moved the heavens
such that a white rainbow pierced the sun and
Venus eclipsed the Pleiades is
false.
If you strike a bell with chopsticks,
or beat a drum with counting rods,
it won't make a sound,
because what you use to strike
is too small.
Now, a person's form is no more than seven *chǐ* (feet),
and with this seven *chǐ* form, focusing one's spirit
to try to accomplish something,
even if accumulating intense intention,
is like striking a bell with chopsticks or beating a drum with counting rods.
How can it move the heavens?
It's not that the spirit is insincere,
but that what's used to move (heaven) is too small.
Moreover, what one wants to harm is a person;
if the person isn't moved,
how could the heavens be moved instead?
Someone asks:
"Can a person's harmful energy
move each other?"
I reply:
"It cannot."
"Yù Ràng 豫讓 wanted to harm Zhào Xiāngzǐ 趙襄子,
and Xiāngzǐ's 襄子 heart was moved.
Guàn Gāo 貫高 wanted to usurp power from Gāo Zǔ 高祖,
and Gāo Zǔ's 高祖 heart was also moved.
These two men harbored intense spirit,
and therefore both rulers trembled."
It is said:
When calamity is about to arrive,
the body itself already possesses strangeness;
this is not something that ordinary people can influence.
How can this be verified?
Sometimes one encounters a madman on the road,
who wields a blade against oneself;
the madman may not necessarily intend to harm one's person,
yet one's body has already exhibited omens beforehand.
From this, it can be said that
the arrival of omens
is a sign that calamity is impending,
and is not caused by those who intend to harm oneself.
Moreover, a person marked by misfortune who receives an inauspicious divination,
obtains a bad hexagram through casting lots,
sees something unlucky upon exiting the door,
and perceives an aura of calamity through divination.
The aura of calamity appears on the face,
just as white rainbows and Venus appear in the sky.
Changes manifest in the sky,
and omens emerge from people;
the above and below spontaneously,
correspond to each other.
The *Commentary* says:
"Yān Tàizǐ Dān 燕太子丹 paid court to Qin,
but was not allowed to leave.
He requested permission from the King of Qin to return.
The King of Qín held him back
and made an oath with him, saying:
'If the sun rises in the middle of the day again,
if the sky rains millet,
if the crows turn white-headed,
if horses grow horns,
and if the wooden image on the kitchen door grows flesh feet,
then you may return.'
At that time,
Heaven aided him,
and the sun rose in the middle of the day again,
the sky rained millet,
the crows turned white-headed,
horses grew horns,
and the wooden image on the kitchen door grew flesh feet.
The King of Qín considered it a miracle
and allowed him to return."
This saying is false.
What kind of person was Yān Tàizǐ Dān 燕太子丹?
How could he move Heaven?
Even when a sage is imprisoned,
cannot move Heaven.
Tàizǐ Dān, a worthy man,
how could he bring this about?
If Heaven could bless the Prince,
causing auspicious signs to arise and thus deliver him,
then it could harmonize with the Qín King's intentions, thereby resolving his difficulties.
Securing one easy thing is easy,
but producing five auspicious signs is difficult.
To abandon the easy task of one thing,
in favor of the difficult task of five things,
why would Heaven not fear the effort?
Tāng was trapped in the Xià Terrace,
Wén Wáng was imprisoned in Yǒulǐ,
Kǒngzǐ was beset in Chén and Cài.
The troubles of these three sages,
Heaven could not help,
to make those who confined them see the blessings and know their sanctity,
and release them to be honored.
Someone might say:
"Those who confined the three sages did not make a vow to them,
the hearts of the three sages were unwilling,
therefore, the auspicious signs blessing the sages had no reason to appear.
Heaven's blessing of people
is like lending people objects or tools;
if people do not seek or request them,
then they will not be given."
I say:
When the Prince desired auspicious signs throughout the land,
豈有語言乎？ [Qǐ yǒu yǔyán hū?] Could there be language (to describe it)?
心願而已。 [Xīnyuàn éryǐ.] It is only a matter of the heart's desires.
然 Tāng 閉於夏臺、 [Rán Tāng bì yú Xiàtái,] However, when Tāng was imprisoned in the Terrace of Xià,
文王拘於羑里時， [Wén Wáng jū yú Yǒulǐ shí,] and King Wén was detained in Yǒulǐ,
心亦願出； [xīn yì yuàn chū;] their hearts also desired to be released;
孔子厄陳、蔡， [Kǒngzǐ è Chén, Cài,] when Kǒngzǐ was in distress in Chén and Cài,
心願食。 [xīn yuàn shí.] his heart desired food.
天何不令夏臺、羑里關鑰毀敗， [Tiān hé bù lìng Xiàtái, Yǒulǐ guānyào huǐbài,] Why did Heaven not cause the locks and keys of the Terrace of Xià and Yǒulǐ to be destroyed and broken,
湯、文涉出； [Tāng, Wén shè chū;] so that Tāng and King Wén could escape?
雨粟陳、蔡， [Yǔ sù Chén, Cài,] Why did it not rain millet in Chén and Cài,
孔子食飽乎？ [Kǒngzǐ shí bǎo hū?] so that Kǒngzǐ could eat his fill?
太史公曰： [Tàishǐgōng yuē:] The Grand Historian said:
「世稱太子丹之令 [Shì chēng Tàizǐ Dān zhī lìng] "The world claims that the order of Crown Prince Dān
天雨粟，馬生角， [tiān yǔ sù, mǎ shēng jiǎo,] caused Heaven to rain millet and horses to grow horns;
大抵皆虛言也。」 [dàdǐ jiē xūyán yě."] for the most part, these are all false statements."
太史公、書漢世實事之人， [Tàishǐgōng, shū Hàn shì shíshì zhī rén,] The Grand Historian, a person who recorded true events of the Hàn dynasty,
而云「虛言」， [ér yún "xūyán",] and yet he says "false statements";
近非實也。 [jìn fēi shí yě.] this is likely not true.
《傳書》言： [《Chuánshū》 yán:] The *Chuánshū* (a lost commentary on the *Shījīng*) says:
「杞梁氏之妻嚮城而哭， [“Qǐ Liángshì zhī qī xiàng chéng ér kū,] "The wife of Qǐ Liángshì faced the city and wept,
城為之崩。」 [chéng wèi zhī bēng."] and the city walls collapsed for her."
此言杞梁 [Cǐ yán Qǐ Liáng] This says that Qǐ Liáng
從軍不還， [cóngjūn bù hái,] went to war and did not return,
其妻痛之， [qí qī tòng zhī,] his wife grieved for him,
嚮城而哭， [xiàng chéng ér kū,] faced the city and wept,
至誠悲痛， [zhìchéng bēitòng,] with utmost sincerity and sorrow,
精氣動城， [jīngqì dòng chéng,] her vital essence moved the city,
故城為之崩也。 [gù chéng wèi zhī bēng yě.] therefore, the city walls collapsed for her.
夫言嚮城而哭者， [Fú yán xiàng chéng ér kū zhě,] Now, saying that she faced the city and wept,
實也； [shí yě;] is true;
言城為之崩者， [yán chéng wèi zhī bēng zhě,] saying that the city walls collapsed for her,
虛也。 [xū yě.] is false.
Of those who cry from grief, none surpasses Yōngmén Zǐ.
Yōngmén Zǐ cried in response to Mèngcháng Jūn,
and Mèngcháng Jūn felt sorrow for him in the city.
Indeed, the sincerity of the weeping
is why those who responded to it felt distressed and deeply moved.
Yōngmén Zǐ could move the heart of Mèngcháng,
but could not move the clothing of Mèngcháng,
because clothing does not know empathy
and does not connect with human feelings.
Now, city walls are made of earth,
and earth is like clothing;
it has no inner feelings.
How could it collapse from sorrow and deep emotion caused by weeping?
If the sound of utter sincerity could move city walls,
then if one cried towards forests and trees,
could they break grass and shatter wood?
If one wept towards water and fire,
could they cause water to gush forth or extinguish fire?
Grass, trees, water, and fire are no different from earth;
yet Qǐliáng's wife could not collapse the city walls,
which is clear.
Perhaps the city walls happened to collapse on their own,
and Qǐliáng's wife happened to be crying;
later generations love falsehood,
not seeking the truth of the matter.
Therefore, the reputation of collapsing the city walls
has not been extinguished to this day.
The *Traditionary Book* says:
"Zōu Yǎn was innocent,
but was imprisoned in Yān.
In the fifth month of summer,
he looked up to the sky and sighed,
and the heavens caused frost to fall."
This is no different from Qǐ Liáng's wife weeping and the city wall collapsing.
There is no difference.
The statement that he was innocently imprisoned
and sighed to the heavens in summer is a fact;
it is real.
The statement that the heavens caused frost to fall for him
is false; it is not real.
Even if ten thousand people raised their voices and all expressed sighs of grief,
they still would not be able to move Heaven.
How could Zōu Yǎn, alone, unjustly wronged, with but one sigh,
cause frost to fall?
Zōu Yǎn's injustice
was no more than that of Zēng Zǐ and Bó Qí.
Zēng Zǐ was doubted and chanted,
Bó Qí was expelled and sang.
Doubt, expulsion, and imprisonment are the same,
chanting, singing, and sighing are equivalent,
Zēng Zǐ and Bó Qí could not bring about cold,
Zōu Yǎn, what kind of person was he,
that he alone could make it rain frost?
The injustice of being expelled
is still not enough to speak of.
Shēn Shēng submitted to the sword,
Zǐ Xū cut his own throat,
were truly filial but were given death,
were truly loyal but were executed,
and moreover, at the time of death, both had vocal utterances.
These utterances, once spoken,
were no different from sighing to the heavens,
but the heavens were not moved for these two men,
only for Zōu Yǎn were they moved,
could it be that heaven is pained to see imprisonment,
but not saddened by bloodshed?
Bó Qí's grievance and pain were similar,
but the moving of heaven was different?
Now, to dry with a single torch, to heat with a single cauldron of water,
it will not become hot all day;
to lean on a one-foot ice block, to place it in the kitchen,
it will not become cold all night.
Why is this?
Small sensations cannot move great things.
Now, Zōu Yǎn's 鄒衍 sigh,
is nothing more than like a torch or a foot of ice,
while the majestic heavens are vast,
not merely the ugly things in a cauldron or kitchen.
If one looks up to the sky and sighs,
the heavens cause frost to fall,
why are the heavens so easily moved,
and the frost so easily brought down?
Alas, sorrow and joy are the same,
happiness and anger are equal.
Yǎn 衍 raised resentment and pain,
causing frost to descend on the world,
causing Yǎn 衍 to receive unwarranted rewards.
If he looks up to the sky and laughs,
can he, in the winter season, make the heavens warm?
The school of "change and return" says:
"If the ruler bestows rewards in autumn, then it becomes warm,
if he inflicts punishments in summer, then it becomes cold."
If cold does not accumulate, then frost will not fall;
if warmth does not last for days, then ice will not melt.
If one man is wronged and sighs once,
the heavens immediately send down frost,
why are the atmospheric conditions so easily changed,
and the seasons so easily reversed?
Cold and warmth each have their own time,
which does not accord with the sayings of the school of "change and return."
Moreover, according to the theory of "change and return,"
perhaps the King of Yān 燕 was fond of using punishments at that time,
Cold air should arrive;
and Yǎn was imprisoned and sighed,
as he sighed, frost just then descended.
The world saw that as he sighed, frost descended,
and therefore said that Zōu Yǎn's sigh caused it.
The *Chuánshū* says:
"Shī Kuàng played the tune of 《Báixuě》 (White Snow),
and divine beings descended because of it,
wind and rain violently arrived,
Duke Píng suffered from illness because of it,
the state of Jìn became red earth."
Some say: "Shī Kuàng's tune of 《Qīngjiǎo》 (Clear Horn),
once played,
clouds rose from the northwest;
played again,
a great wind arrived,
heavy rain followed,
tearing the curtains,
breaking the sacrificial vessels,
and dislodging the tiles from the corridors.
Those seated scattered and fled,
Duke Píng was fearful,
hiding in a side room of the corridor.
The state of Jìn suffered a great drought,
red earth for three years,
Duke Píng suffered from illness."
Now, 《Báixuě》 and 《Qīngjiǎo》,
are perhaps the same tune with different names,
their calamities and failures are essentially the same.
The families who transmit the *Chuánshū*,
record it as true;
the common people observing,
and believe it to be so.
Examining the actual truth,
[it] is likely empty words.
Now, what kind of sound is "Qīng Jiǎo"
that it can cause this?
[They] say:
"'Qīng Jiǎo' is a wood sound,
therefore it causes wind and rain.
Like wood creating wind,
rain and wind come together."
Three feet of wood,
the sound of several strings,
moving heaven and earth,
how miraculous is that?
This is just like one cry collapsing a city,
one sigh causing frost to fall, and such things.
Shī Kuàng was able to play "Qīng Jiǎo,"
he must have received instruction,
he wasn't able to naturally produce it.
When he first received instruction,
he practiced day and night,
not just playing it once or twice.
If we thoroughly examine the words in the *Zhuàn Shū*,
when Shī Kuàng learned "Qīng Jiǎo",
wind and rain should have arrived then.
The "Record of Transmissions" says:
"When Hù Bā played the zither,
the fish in the deep came out to listen;
when Shī Kuàng played the qin,
the six horses raised their heads and ate no more."
Some say:
"When Shī Kuàng played "Qīngjiǎo,"
at the first performance,
there were sixteen black cranes, coming from the south,
gathering on the high part of the gate porch;
at the second performance, they lined up;
at the third performance,
they stretched their necks and cried,
spread their wings and danced,
their sound matched the *gōng* and *shāng* tones,
their cries echoed to the heavens.
Lord Píng was greatly pleased,
and all who were present rejoiced."
The *Book of Documents* says:
"Strike the stones, pat the stones,
and all the beasts will dance."
Although this is strange and wonderful,
it is still believable.
Why is that?
Birds and beasts love mournful sounds,
and their ears are the same as human ears.
When birds and beasts see that people want to eat,
they also want to eat them,
When they hear human joy,
why wouldn't they also be joyful?
However, the stories of "fish listening," "horses grazing upwards," "black cranes stretching their necks," and "all beasts dancing together"
are probably true to some extent.
But the stories of wind and rain arriving, the state of Jìn 晉 experiencing a great drought,
the land being red for three years, and Píng Gōng 平公 suffering from paralysis
are likely fabrications.
Perhaps when the *Qīng Jiǎo* 清角 melody was played,
there happened to be wind and rain,
and after the wind and rain,
the state of Jìn 晉 coincidentally experienced a drought.
Píng Gōng 平公 loved music
and laughed excessively,
and coincidentally developed paralysis.
The families who transmit these stories
believed them to be true,
and when people in the world saw them,
they came to regard them as facts.
In reality, the music cannot bring about such things.
How can we verify this?
Violent wind and rain storms
This is the disorder of *yin* and *yang*.
If music can disrupt *yin* and *yang*,
then it can also regulate *yin* and *yang*.
What need then for a ruler to cultivate himself and rectify his conduct,
and broadly implement benevolent policies?
Just have the drums play tunes that regulate *yin* and *yang*,
and harmonious *qi* will arrive naturally,
and peace will establish itself.
The *Commentary to the Book [of Documents]* says:
"Tāng encountered a seven-year drought,
and prayed with his body in Sānglín,
blaming himself for six faults,
and then heaven rained."
Some say: "Five years.
The prayer said:
'If I, the one man, am guilty,
let it not extend to the myriad people;
if the myriad people are guilty,
let it rest on me, the one man.
Heaven must not, because of the lack of diligence of one man,
cause God and the spirits to harm the lives of the people.'
Thereupon he cut his hair,
bound his hands,
and regarded himself as a sacrificial animal,
to pray for blessings to God.
God was greatly pleased,
and timely rain then arrived."
If we say that Tāng prayed in the Mulberry Forest, blaming himself,
like saying he cut his hair and adorned his hands,
considering himself a sacrificial offering,
to pray for blessings from the Supreme Deity,
then that is true.
But to say that the rain came
because Tāng blamed himself and prayed with his body,
that is probably a fabrication.
When Kǒngzǐ fell ill,
Zǐlù asked to offer prayers.
Kǒngzǐ said:
"Is there such a thing?"
Zǐlù said:
"Yes, there is;
the *Lěi* [Funeral Oration] says:
'Pray to you, the gods above and below.'"
Kǒngzǐ said:
"Qiū's prayers have been for a long time."
The sage cultivates his person and rectifies his conduct;
his customary prayers have been for a long time.
Heaven and earth, spirits and gods,
know that he is without guilt,
therefore he said, "Prayed for a long time."
The *Yì* [Book of Changes] says:
"The great person unites his virtue with Heaven and Earth,
unites his brightness with the sun and moon,
unites his order with the four seasons,
"To unite with the spirits in their auspiciousness and misfortune."
This speaks of the sage being of the same virtue and conduct as Heaven and Earth and the spirits.
That one must pray to obtain blessings
indicates that they are not the same.
Tāng and Kǒngzǐ were both sages,
both of whom prayed regularly for a long time.
Kǒngzǐ did not have Zǐlù pray to cure illness,
so how could Tāng obtain rain through prayer?
Kǒngzǐ prayed regularly,
yet he still suffered from illness;
Tāng also prayed regularly,
yet the year still experienced a great drought.
Thus, Heaven and Earth having floods and droughts
is like people having illnesses.
Illnesses cannot be removed by self-reproach,
and floods and droughts cannot be dispelled by prayers of apology;
this is clear.
Did Tāng cause the drought
due to some transgression?
That would mean he is not of the same virtue as Heaven and Earth.
If it wasn't caused by transgression,
then self-reproach and prayers of apology
are also of no benefit.
A human form is seven feet tall,
within the form are the five constant virtues,
and one can have a feverish illness.
Even with deep self-reproach,
one still cannot be cured.
How much more so with the vastness of Heaven,
which has its own changes of floods and droughts?
How can Tāng, using his seven-foot form,
and the sincerity within that form,
remove the drought through self-reproach and prayers of apology?
How could he possibly obtain rain?
A person is on top of a layered terrace,
and people bow their heads beneath the layered terrace,
requesting things from the person on the terrace.
The person on the terrace hears their words,
and then pities them and gives to them;
but if they do not hear their words,
even if they are utterly sincere,
in the end they will obtain nothing.
Now, the distance between Heaven and man,
is not just the height of a layered terrace.
Although Tāng blamed himself,
how could Heaven hear and know and give him rain?
Now, drought is a transformation of fire;
and inundation is a change of water.
Yáo encountered a great flood,
which could be called inundation.
Yáo did not blame himself and use his body to pray,
but necessarily had Shùn and Yǔ control it,
knowing that a water transformation must be controlled.
Eliminating inundation is not done through prayer,
eliminating drought should also be like that.
From this perspective,
Tāng's 湯 prayers could not bring rain.
Sometimes, after a long drought,
the time is right for rain to fall on its own.
Tāng 湯, because of the long drought,
happened to blame himself as well.
People saw the rain fall
following Tāng's 湯 self-blame,
and therefore said that Tāng 湯 obtained rain through prayer.
The *Zhuàn Shū* 傳書 states:
"Cāng Jié 倉頡 made writing,
and the sky rained millet,
and ghosts cried at night."
This means that when literature flourished, disorder gradually appeared,
so the strange phenomena
resulted in the sky raining millet and ghosts crying at night.
Speaking of the sky raining millet and ghosts crying at night,
is a reality.
Saying that it was in response to Cāng Jié's 倉頡 creation of writing,
is false.
Now, the Yellow River produced the *Diagram* (Tú 圖),
and the Luo River produced the *Document* (Shū 書),
these are auspicious responses to sagely emperors and enlightened kings.
The Diagrams and Documents, the writings, how are they different from the writings made by Cāng Jié 倉頡?
Tiāndì wèi túshū, The universe serves as books,
Cāngjié zuò wénzì, Cāngjié created writing,
Yè yǔ tiāndì tóng, His work is the same as that of the universe,
Zhǐ yǔ guǐshén hé, His intent aligns with spirits and deities,
Hé fēi hé è, What is wrong or evil,
Ér zhì yǔ sù, shén kū zhī guài zāi? That it would cause the strange phenomena of rain of millet and weeping spirits?
Shǐ tiāndì guǐshén è rén yǒu shū, If the universe, spirits, and deities hate humans possessing writing,
Zé qí chū túshū Then their production of the universe as books
fēi yě; is wrong;
tiān bù è rén yǒu shū, If the universe does not hate humans possessing writing,
zuò shū hé fēi, ér zhì cǐ guài? What is wrong with creating writing, that it would cause this strangeness?
Huò shí Cāngjié shì zuò shū, Perhaps Cāngjié happened to be creating writing,
tiān shì yǔ sù, The universe happened to rain millet,
guǐ ǒu yè kū, And spirits happened to weep at night,
ér yǔ sù, And the rain of millet,
guǐshén kū, And the weeping of spirits and deities,
zì yǒu suǒ wéi, each had their own reasons,
shì jiàn yìng shū ér zhì, But the world sees them as happening in response to the writing,
zé wèi zuò shū shēng luàn bài zhī xiàng, And thus says that the creation of writing produces omens of chaos and failure,
yìng shì ér dòng yě. And that it responds to events and acts accordingly.
"Tiān yǔ gǔ," "The universe rains grain,"
lùn zhě wèi zhī cóng tiān ér xià, Commentators say it comes from above,
yìng biàn ér shēng. Born in response to change.
Rú yǐ yúnyǔ lùn zhī, If we discuss it in terms of clouds and rain,
yǔ gǔ zhī biàn, The strangeness of the rain of grain,
bùzú guài yě. is not worth wondering at.
How can this be verified?
Now, clouds and rain originate from hills and mountains,
and when they descend and disperse, they become rain.
People see it falling from above,
and so they call it "heaven rains water."
In summer days, it rains water,
in winter days, the weather is cold, so the rain congeals and becomes snow,
all of which originate from the cloud vapor rising from the hills and mountains,
not descending and gathering from the sky onto the earth,
this is clear.
Now, the "rain" of grain
is also because cloud spreads out
and rises from the earth,
consequently blowing together with strong winds,
mixing in the sky,
and gathering on the earth.
People see it falling from the sky,
and so they call it "heaven rains grain."
During the 31st year of the Jiànwǔ reign (of Emperor Guāngwǔ of the Eastern Hàn),
in Chénliú, it rained grain,
and the fallen grain covered the ground.
Upon examining the shape of the grain,
it was like thatch and black,
resembling barnyard millet seeds.
Perhaps at that time, in the land of the Eastern Īdí barbarians,
this grain grew,
but the Īdí barbarians do not eat grains,
so this grain grows in the wilderness,
ripens, and hangs withered to the ground,
then encounters a sudden strong wind,
which blows it up, and it flies along with the wind,
when the wind weakens, the grain gathers and falls onto Zhōngguó (Central China).
Zhōngguó people see it,
and calls it "heaven-rained grain."
How is this like?
A wildfire burns mountains and marshes.
Within the mountains and marshes,
grasses and trees are all burned.
Their leaves become ash.
A sudden violent wind arises,
blows them up,
and they fly up to the sky.
When the wind weakens, the leaves fall down,
gathering on the roads.
The so-called "heaven-rained grain"
is similar to the burnt leaves of grasses and trees flying and gathering.
Yet the world thinks it is rained grain,
and those who write *Chuán Shū* (Commentaries and Records) consider it a strange phenomenon.
Heaven is responsible for dispensing *qì* (vital energy),
and earth is responsible for producing things.
Whatever leaves and fruits can be pecked and eaten
are all produced by the earth,
not done by heaven.
Now, grain is not produced by *qì*.
It requires earth to be formed.
Though it speaks of strange transformations,
strange transformations are based on categories.
Things that are born from the earth
further gather from the heavens.
Things born of the heavens,
can they come from the earth?
The earth's possession of myriad things
is like the heavens' possession of the arrayed stars.
The stars do not newly grow from the earth,
so why should grain alone grow from the heavens?
The *Commentary Book* also says:
"Bó Yì made a well,
dragons ascended to the dark clouds,
spirits dwelled on Kūnlún."
It says that the dragon well was harmful,
therefore the dragons and spirits transformed.
Now, the statement that dragons ascended to the dark clouds
is fact.
The statement that spirits dwelled on Kūnlún,
and further stating it was because of the well making,
that the dragons ascended and the spirits departed,
is fiction.
Now, making wells and drinking
and tilling fields and eating
are both equally factual.
Bó Yì made wells,
resulting in changes.
From the beginning for those who plow and weed,
why are there no changes?
Shénnóng fashioned a curved wood into a plow,
teaching the people to plow and weed,
the people began to eat grains,
grains began to be sown.
Plowing the soil to make fields,
digging the ground to make wells,
wells produce water to relieve thirst,
fields produce grain to relieve hunger,
this is what heaven, earth, ghosts, and spirits desire to do,
why does the dragon ascend the dark clouds?
Why do the gods reside in Kūnlún?
That the dragon ascends the dark clouds,
has existed from ancient times to the present,
it is not that only after Yì made wells that it ascended.
Now it is high summer,
thunder and rain arrive at the proper time,
dragons often ascend the clouds.
Clouds and rain correspond with dragons,
dragons ride on clouds and rain to travel,
things of a kind attract each other,
it is not purposeful.
In Yáo's time,
the world was greatly harmonious,
The people had nothing to do.
There were people, around fifty in number, playing the game of hitting the earth with clods on the road.
Onlookers said:
"How great is the virtue of Yáo!"
The one hitting the clods said:
"I rise at sunrise to work,
and rest at sunset.
I dig a well to drink,
and cultivate the fields to eat.
What power does Yáo have?"
Wells already existed in the time of Yáo.
During the time of the Táng and Yú dynasties,
there were those who raised dragons and those who controlled dragons.
Dragons were always at court.
At the end of the Xià dynasty, when governance declined,
the dragons then went into hiding.
It wasn't because Yì dug wells
that the dragons ascended into the clouds.
What is meant by "divinity"?
What kind of divinity is it?
All the gods are like this;
why would all the gods hate people for digging wells?
If the gods are the same as people,
then they should also have the desire to drink.
If they have the desire to drink,
hating the well and leaving would
not be the truth.
Yì almost certainly did not dig wells;
dragons do not ascend to the clouds for the sake of well-digging;
spirits do not dwell on Kūnlún;
the writings transmitted are intentionally misleading,
intended to deceive future generations.
The *Zhuàn Shū* says:
"Liáng Shān collapsed,
damming the river, preventing it from flowing for three days,
and the Jìn ruler worried about it.
Jìn Bózōng, based on the words of a cart driver,
ordered Jǐng Gōng to wear plain white mourning clothes and weep,
and the river flowed again."
This is a false statement.
The collapse of a mountain damming a river
is like a person having a carbuncle or tumor,
with blood vessels blocked.
Can one treat a carbuncle or tumor
by wearing plain clothes and weeping?
In the time of Yáo,
the great flood reached the sky,
engulfing mountains and flooding hills.
Emperor Yáo sighed and lamented,
widely seeking wise men.
The flood was worse than the river being dammed,
Yáo's worries were deeper than Jǐng Gōng's,
I have not heard that the sound of weeping in plain white silk
can overcome it.
Did Yáo not have the skill of a cart driver?
Even if the flood became great,
could it not be subdued and removed by sound?
Just as "weeping in plain white silk"
is regretting mistakes and blaming oneself,
Yáo and Yǔ's control of the floods was through physical labor,
not self-blame.
Mount Liáng,
was Mount Yáo's time;
the blocked river,
was the river in Yáo's time.
The mountain collapses and the river is blocked,
heaven rains and water surges,
the changes in these two are not different.
Yáo and Yǔ controlled the floods with physical labor,
the cart driver controlled the blocked river by blaming himself,
the changes are the same but the control is different,
people are equal but the responses are different,
it is probably not the essence of sages and their transformative recovery.
Generally speaking, the principle of transformative recovery,
that which can move each other,
is based on the category of things.
When there is cold, restore it with warmth,
warmth can be relieved with cold.
Therefore, using dragons to bring rain,
and using punishments to drive away heat,
are all based on the qi of the Five Elements,
using them to mutually influence and overcome each other.
If a mountain collapses and blocks a river,
to wear white mourning clothes and weep for it,
what meaning is there in this principle?
Perhaps this was when the river was blocked,
and the mountain had just collapsed,
the earth had accumulated,
and the water had not yet surged.
After three days,
the water surged, the earth scattered, gradually breaking down and crumbling.
As it broke down and crumbled, the water flowed,
finally flowing eastward.
They encountered the words of someone who obtained the carriage of Bó Zōng,
and because of the white mourning clothes, they wept,
they wept because of the flow,
and when it flowed, they said the river's change started from this and recovered.
But in reality, it is not so.
How to verify this?
If the mountain were to constantly collapse by itself?
Wearing white mourning clothes and weeping would be of no benefit.
If it is a heavenly change that responds to it,
one should change the governance.
Wearing white mourning clothes and weeping,
what governance is being changed, so that the heavenly change would be reversed?
The "Commentary on the Book of Documents" says:
"Zēngzǐ's 曾子 filial piety
was such that he shared the same vital energy (qì) with his mother.
Zēngzǐ 曾子 went to the fields to gather firewood.
A guest arrived and wanted to leave.
Zēngmǔ 曾母 said:
'I wish to keep him here;
Shēn 參 will arrive soon.'
And she immediately used her right hand to squeeze her left arm.
Zēngzǐ's 曾子 left arm immediately felt pain.
He immediately rushed back, and asked his mother
saying: 'Why does my arm hurt?'
His mother said:
'Just now, a guest came and wanted to leave,
so I squeezed my arm to call you back.'
This is because, with utmost filial piety,
he shared the same vital energy with his parents;
if their bodies had an illness,
his spirit would immediately sense it."
Someone said:
"This is false."
The saying, "The utmost of filial piety and fraternal love
reaches the spirits and deities,"
means that virtuous transformation reaches Heaven and Earth.
Vulgar people, following this line of reasoning, say,
that in the utmost state of filial piety and fraternal love,
essence and vital energy interact.
If Zēng Mǔ's arm ached,
Zēng Zǐ's arm would also ache.
If Zēng Mǔ was sick, would Zēng Zǐ also be sick?
If Zēng Mǔ died,
would Zēng Zǐ also die?
Examining the matter,
Zēng Mǔ died first,
and Zēng Zǐ did not die.
This shows that vital essence can slightly affect each other,
but cannot greatly influence each other.
People say that Shēn Xǐ heard his mother singing at night,
and his heart was moved.
He opened the gate and asked who was singing,
and it was indeed his mother.
Because he heard his mother's voice,
voices can affect each other,
his heart was saddened and his intentions stirred.
He opened the gate and asked,
which was the real reason.
Now, if Zēng Mǔ is at home,
and Zēng Zǐ is in the field,
and he doesn't hear the sound of her calling,
how can his mother slightly pinching her arm,
possibly affect her son?
I suspect that people are praising and embellishing,
having heard that Zēng Zǐ's filial piety is unmatched in the world,
and thus fabricated the story of the mother pinching her arm.
It is commonly said:
Zhuó Gōng of Nányáng, when serving as magistrate of Gōushì,
locusts did not enter his boundary.
The reason given is that, due to his virtuousness and utmost sincerity,
calamitous insects did not enter his county.
This is again a fallacy.
The transformative power of virtuousness and utmost sincerity
communicates with those of the same kind,
enabling mutual understanding,
and then admiration and submission.
Locusts and
horseflies are of a different category.
How could they know or perceive and be aware of Zhuó Gōng's transformative influence?
If a virtuous person were to live deep in the wilderness,
would horseflies not enter their dwelling?
If horseflies cannot avoid the dwelling of a virtuous person,
how could locusts not enter Zhuó Gōng's county?
If one were to say that locusts are different and distinct from horseflies,
then cold and heat are also calamitous changes.
If an entire commandery is cold,
and a virtuous person governs one county within it,
could the boundary of that one county alone be warm?
If cold and heat cannot avoid the county of a virtuous person,
how could locusts not enter Zhuó Gōng's boundary?
Therefore,
If locusts happened not to enter the border,
and if Zhuō Gōng's reputation for virtue was occasionally praised in the world,
the world would then say he was able to ward off locusts.
How can this be verified?
When locusts gather in the fields,
they cannot universally and broadly cover all the land;
they often accumulate in large or small quantities in certain places.
The land where they do not accumulate,
is perhaps where Dào Zhí resided;
the fields where they are scarce,
is perhaps where Bó Yí lived.
Passing through, accumulating in large or small quantities,
cannot completely cover everything.
The amount of land they accumulate on,
means that passing through the county there will be some that leave or remain.
Quantity
cannot be used to verify good or evil,
presence or absence
how can it clarify virtue and wickedness?
It is simply that the locusts passed by of their own accord,
it is not because a virtuous person's border was not entered, this is clear.

The world argues that those who do good will have fortune arrive,

people act,

hidden benevolence,
Heaven and Earth repay the virtue.

to show that virtue is rewarded;

how can one actually obtain blessings?

There was a man of Sòng who liked to do good deeds,

Kǒngzǐ said:

use it to make offerings to the spirits."

After a year,
his father went blind for no reason.

"It is auspicious,

Heaven's anger is roaring and sighing;

The *Lǐ* (Book of Rites) says:

One goes out and one goes in,

The shape of the engaging pivots,

This is an imitation of its kind.
When the qi mutually engages as pivots and splits apart,

The sound of a sudden, tearing rip,

If the qi shoots and hits a person,

The truthful explanation
of thunder is that it is the excited qi of the sun.
How is this made clear?
In the first month, *yáng* moves,
therefore thunder begins in the first month.
In the fifth month, *yáng* is at its peak,
therefore thunder is rapid in the fifth month.
In autumn and winter, *yáng* declines,

During the height of summer,
the sun is in charge,
and *yīn qì* invades it.
When Yīnyáng separate and contend,
they then mutually clash and rub.
Clashing and rubbing then causes spurting forth.
Spurting forth creates poison.
If it hits a person, they immediately die.
If it hits a tree, the tree breaks.
If it hits a house, the house collapses.
If a person is under a tree or between houses,

How can this be verified?
Try pouring a *dǒu* of water onto fire used for smelting and casting.
The vapor violently bursts apart,

If one is close to it,

Heaven and earth act as a furnace, how vast!
Yángqì acts as fire, how fierce!

If separation and contention spurts forth,

If it hits and wounds a person's body,

When smelting workers melt iron,

If it is dry, the iron goes down smoothly.

If it sprays and hits a person's body,

The heat of the yang energy

the yin energy striking it

the striking energy hitting people

Now, thunder

If the marks from the burn look like writing,

If all people have transgressions,

clearly writing out the reason for the punishment,

The "Chart" emerged from the Yellow River,

Lightning writing is not evident,

If that is the case,
the traces of fire burning

Perhaps some people add to what exists,

Vain and deceitful customs
love to create strange and bizarre things.
How to verify that lightning is fire?
If a person is struck by lightning and dies,
examine their body immediately.
If the head is struck, then the beard and hair will be burnt.
If the body is struck, then the skin will be scorched.
Stand over the corpse and smell the scent of fire -

Practitioners of Daoist arts believe that lightning

When a person is harmed by the cold,

the abdomen, being originally warm,

this is the third proof.
During a thunderstorm,
flashes of lightning are frequently seen,
and a large fire, like a person shining,
is the fourth proof.
When lightning strikes,
at that time,
it sometimes burns down people's houses and even the grass and trees on the ground –
this is the fifth proof.
Thus, the argument that thunder is fire has five proofs;
the claim that thunder is the anger of Heaven has no evidence whatsoever.
Therefore, the idea that thunder is the anger of Heaven
is empty and false.
Someone might object, saying:

What the *Lunyu* (Analects) refers to,
what the *Liji* speaks of,

Why is this?
Because it is not for oneself.
If indeed one fears thunder,
it is also not sufficient to emulate punishing hidden wrongdoings.
Why is this?
What the thunder strikes
is mostly people without fault.
The gentleman fears encountering it by chance,

Now, if this is the case,
the gentleman's movements

Indiscriminate strikes do not punish wrongdoing,

The King of Sòng asked Táng Yāng,

To punish all those who are not good.

The King of Sòng recklessly inflicted punishments,

The *Rú Shū* (Book of the Confucians) says:

One like Lú Áo.

and at the time, everyone saw it.
Yet even in Confucian texts, there are still those who say he attained the Dao and ascended to immortality,
with his chickens and dogs ascending to heaven as well.
How much more likely then, that Lú Áo 盧敖, all alone,
in a place where he walked alone and left no traces,
would fabricate empty and mysterious words?
This is no different from the words of Xiàng Màndū 項曼都 of Púbǎn 蒲坂 in Hédōng 河東.
Màndū 曼都 loved the Dao and studied immortality,
He abandoned his family and disappeared.
After three years, he returned.
His family asked about his condition,
and Màndū said:
"When I left, I was unaware of myself.
Suddenly, I seemed to be lying down,
and there were several immortals
who took me up to the heavens,
stopping a few *lǐ* away from the moon.
I saw the moon above and below in darkness.
The darkness lacked any sense of direction.
Dwelling beside the moon,
the cold was terribly bleak.
My mouth was hungry and wanted to eat,
so the immortals would give me a cup of flowing nectar.
Each time I drank a cup,
I wouldn't be hungry for months.
I don't know how many years and months passed.
I don't know what I did to get here.
Suddenly, I seemed to be lying down,
The people of Hédōng called him a dismissed immortal.
Those who are truly knowledgeable heard of it,
and knew it was not so.
If Màndū could ascend to the heavens,
why wasn't he an immortal?
He was gone for three years.
what reason would he have to return?
When a person departs from the human realm,
and ascends above the celestial heavens,
their essence, vital energy, and physical form
will undergo changes compared to their former state.
All things undergo transformation and change,
and never return to their original state.
Fù Yù (復育) transformed into a cicada;
once its wings were fully formed,
and I came back down here."
it could not transform back into Fù Yù (復育).
Things that can ascend
all possess wings;
if they ascend and then descend again,
their wings remain the same.
Have you seen wings on Màn Dū's (曼都) body?
If so, then your words are believable.
If his body has no wings,
then your words are false and absurd.
If they are false, then he is the same as Lú Áo (盧敖) in reality.
Perhaps Màn Dū (曼都) admired the Dao,
secretly abandoned his family and left,
Zhōu Zhāng 周章 journeyed afar.
In the end, he gained nothing.
His strength exhausted, his hopes reaching their limit,
he silently returned home.
Ashamed and without words,
he then spoke of Heaven.
His meaning was to say that the Dao could be learned,
that there truly were immortals,
and that he himself probably had transgressed in some way,
therefore, it was accomplished and then rejected,
raised up and then brought down.
The Rú Shū 儒書 (Confucian texts) say:
The King of Qí 齊 suffered from a disease of wasting.
He sent a man to Sòng 宋 to welcome Wén Zhì 文摯.
Wén Zhì 文摯 arrived,
observed the King's disease,
and said to the Prince:
"The King's disease
can certainly be cured.
However,
when the King's disease is cured,
he will surely kill Zhì 摯."
The Prince said:
"Why?"
Wén Zhì 文摯 replied:
"If the King is not angered,
then the disease cannot be cured.
If the King is angered,
then Zhì 摯 will surely die."
The Prince kowtowed and earnestly pleaded, saying:
"If only you can cure the King's disease,
your servant and your servant's mother will contend with death before the King,
the King will surely have pity on your servant and your servant's mother.
I hope sir will not worry."
Wén Zhì said:
"Yes,
I am willing to risk death for the King."
He made an appointment with the Crown Prince,
intending to go, but failed to arrive three times,
the King of Qí was already very angry.
Wén Zhì arrived,
without removing his shoes, he stepped onto the bed, trampling on the King's clothes,
and inquired about the King's illness.
The King was angry and did not speak to him.
Wén Zhì then deliberately said things to further enrage the King.
The King shouted and got up,
and his illness was thus cured.
The King was furious and displeased,
and wanted to boil Wén Zhì alive.
The Crown Prince and the Queen urgently argued against it, but to no avail,
and they indeed boiled Wén Zhì alive in a cauldron.
They cooked him for three days and three nights,
but his color did not change.
Wén Zhì said:
"If you truly want to kill me,
Then why not cover it,
to cut off the *yīn* and *yáng* energies?"
The king had it covered,
and Wén Zhì then died.
Now, Wén Zhì,
was said to be a *dào* practitioner,
who would not get wet in water
or burn in fire.
Therefore, being in a cauldron for three days and three nights,
his complexion did not change.
This is a false claim.
If Wén Zhì, boiled for three days and three nights,
did not change color,
and died from having it covered, cutting off his breath,
that is not evidence of attaining the *Dào*.
All living things
die when their breath is cut off;
dead things
rot when cooked.
If you put a living thing in a sealed container,
cover its mouth,
and seal the cracks with lacquer,
so that the inner and outer air are separated,
and its breath cannot escape,
it will die in a short time.
If you put it in a cauldron of boiling water,
will also immediately decompose.
Why?
Because the body and qi are the same,
receiving their nature from Heaven,
sharing a common category.
Could Wén Zhì not breathe?
Being the same as metal and stone,
entering boiling water without rotting,
that is correct;
if Wén Zhì can breathe,
then boiling him does not cause death,
that is incorrect.
If Wén Zhì can speak,
speaking uses sound,
and sound uses breathing.
The movement of breathing
depends on the generation of blood and qi.
The generation of blood and qi
relies on bones and flesh.
Being things of bone and flesh,
boiling them will cause death.
Now saying that boiling him does not cause death
is the first falsity.
Since he can be boiled and not die,
he is a True Man,
the same as metal and stone.
Metal and stone, even if covered,
To claim there is no difference is no different from not covering it up.
Now, to say that Wén Zhì died when covered,
is the second falsehood.
Place a person in cold water,
without the heat of soup or fire,
the nose and mouth, not connected to the outside,
in a short while,
their breath will be cut off and they will die.
Submerging a person in cold water,
they would still not be able to live,
how much more so in boiling soup,
with the intensity of a fierce fire?
To say he entered the soup and did not die,
is the third falsehood.
When a person is submerged in water,
their mouth is not visible from the outside,
their voice does not rise.
When cooking Wén Zhì,
his body must have been submerged in the cauldron. Submerged, then the mouth is not visible,
and if the mouth is not visible, then the voice does not rise.
The words of Wén Zhì,
is the fourth falsehood.
To cook a person who immediately dies,
for three days and three nights,
and their complexion does not change,
even a foolish person,
would still know to be surprised by this.
Even if the King of Qí was ignorant,
Tàizǐ and the assembled ministers should have perceived his extraordinary qualities.
If they found Wén Zhì strange and unusual,
then they should have requested that he be treated with respect and honor,
and followed him to inquire about the Dao.
Now, it is said that for three days and three nights,
there was no word from any minister requesting his release;
this is the fifth falsehood.
It may be that they occasionally heard of Wén Zhì being truly cooked,
and that he died immediately upon being cooked.
People then saw Wén Zhì as a man of the Dao,
and thus fabricated the tale of his immortality.
It is like the fact that Huángdì actually died,
but the tradition says he ascended to heaven;
Huáinán was condemned for rebellion,
but the records say he transcended the world.
The world loves to transmit falsehoods,
and so the story of Wén Zhì has been passed down to this day.
The world does not witness the effectiveness of attaining the Dao,
but there are people who live long lives.
When the world sees long-lived people,
they study the Dao to become immortals,
and live beyond a hundred years without dying;
everyone calls them immortals.
How can this be made clear?
For example, during the time of Emperor Wǔ,
there was Lǐ Shǎo Jūn, who presented himself to the emperor with methods of worshiping the stove, abstaining from grains, and warding off old age,
The emperor respected him.
Shǎo Jūn concealed his age and place of birth,
always claiming to be seventy years old,
and that he could manipulate objects and reverse aging.
He traveled around to the various lords using his arts.
He had no wife or children.
People heard that he could manipulate objects and not age,
and further presented him with gifts, so he always had surplus money, gold, clothing, and food.
People all thought he did not manage property and yet was generously supplied,
and also did not know where he was from,
so they increasingly believed him and vied to serve him.
Shǎo Jūn by nature loved methods [of immortality],
and was good at ingenious predictions that hit the mark surprisingly.
He once drank with the Marquis of Wǔ'ān,
and among those seated was someone over ninety years old,
Shǎo Jūn then said that he had traveled with that person's grandfather to a place where they shot birds.
When the old man was a child,
he followed his grandfather
and recognized the place.
Everyone at the gathering was completely astonished.
Shǎo Jūn met with the emperor,
and the emperor had an ancient bronze vessel,
and asked Shǎo Jūn about it.
Shǎo Jūn said:
"This vessel was placed in the cypress chamber in the fifteenth year of Duke Huán of Qí."
Afterwards, examining its inscription,
it was indeed a vessel of Duke Huán of Qí,
the entire palace was astonished,
thinking Shǎo Jūn was a spirit, a man of several hundred years.
After a long time,
Shǎo Jūn died of illness.
The so-called people who have attained the Dao in this age
are of the kind of Lǐ Shǎo Jūn.
